title: US Senate Republicans block a national security package including Ukraine aid
body:
On Wednesday, 6 December 2023, Senate Republicans blocked a 110 billion dollar national security funding package from advancing. The package covered wartime funding for Ukraine and Israel and other national security priorities, including tens of billions of dollars in military and economic aid for Ukraine. Every Republican senator voted against advancing it. Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer called the failed vote a sad night in the history of the Senate and the country.

Republicans wanted changes to US border policy before approving the aid. Senators had reportedly agreed on raising the initial standard for migrants to enter the asylum system but remained divided over limits on humanitarian parole. House Speaker Mike Johnson said he would not support the aid package unless it adhered to H.R. 2, a bill with conservative immigration priorities.

President Joe Biden, speaking at the White House the same day, called Republican tactics stunning and dangerous. He warned of dire consequences for Ukraine and a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin if Congress failed to pass the package, and said he was willing to make significant compromises on the border. The White House warned that Ukraine's military could stall or be overrun without more funding soon. According to the Associated Press report, the path through Congress for the emergency funds was rapidly disappearing, with only a handful of days left in Washington before the end of the year.
